title: Chole Bhature
description: Chole Bhature is a beloved North Indian combination of spicy, tangy chickpea curry served with hot, fluffy, deep-fried bhature. Slow-simmered chole is enriched with whole spices, chole masala, and a finishing touch of butter or ghee, while the bhature are made with yogurt-leavened dough for a soft, puffy texture.

ingredients.title: For the Chole (Chickpea Curry)
items: Chickpeas (Kabuli Chana) – 1½ cups, soaked overnight for about 8 hours

ingredients.title: Ground Spices
items: Regular red chili powder – ½ tsp
Chole masala – 2 tsp, store-bought or homemade

ingredients.title: For the Bhature
items: Oil – 2 tsp, plus more for frying

instruction.title: Step 1 – Cooking the Chole
steps: Drain the soaked chickpeas and add them to a pressure cooker or Instant Pot with fresh water, the tea bag, and salt.
Cook until the chickpeas are soft but still hold their shape.
Discard the tea bag after cooking.
Heat oil or ghee in a deep pan and add the bay leaf, black cardamom, green cardamoms, cinnamon, cloves, and cumin seeds. Let them crackle.
Add chopped onions and sauté until golden brown.
Add ginger-garlic paste and slit green chilies. Sauté for about 1 minute.
Add tomato puree and cook until the oil separates from the masala.

instruction.title: Step 2 – Building the Chole Masala
steps: Add Kashmiri red chili powder, regular red chili powder, coriander powder, turmeric powder, roasted cumin powder, and chole masala.
Cook the spices for 3–4 minutes, stirring regularly.
Add the boiled chickpeas along with some of their cooking water.
Simmer for 20–25 minutes until the curry becomes thick, glossy, and flavorful.
Finish with butter, garam masala, amchur, and fresh coriander leaves.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Preparing the Bhature Dough
steps: Combine maida, sooji, salt, sugar, baking powder, and baking soda in a large bowl.
Add whisked yogurt and oil and mix well.
Gradually add warm water and knead into a soft dough.
Knead for 8–10 minutes until the dough becomes smooth.
Cover and let the dough rest for at least 2 hours.

instruction.title: Step 4 – Rolling and Frying the Bhature
steps: Divide the rested dough into equal-sized balls.
Roll each ball into an oval or round disc.
Heat oil to about 190°C (375°F).
Carefully slide the rolled dough into the hot oil.
Fry until the bhatura puffs up and becomes golden brown, turning as needed.
Remove and drain excess oil.

instruction.title: Step 5 – Plating and Serving
steps: Serve hot chole in a deep bowl.
Top or garnish with onion rings, green chili, a lemon wedge, and fresh coriander.
Serve freshly fried bhature alongside the chole.
Optionally serve with pickled onions, mint chutney, or boondi raita.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Serve hot chole with freshly fried, fluffy bhature.
Garnish with onion rings, green chilies, lemon wedges, and fresh coriander.
Pair with pickled onions, mint chutney, or boondi raita.
For a restaurant-style finish, add a spoonful of ghee and a squeeze of lime to the chole just before serving.

chefTips: Soak the chickpeas overnight to ensure they cook evenly and become tender.
The optional tea bag gives the chole its characteristic deep color; remove it after pressure cooking.
Cook the onion-tomato masala until the oil separates before adding the chickpeas for deeper flavor.
Rest the bhatura dough for at least 2 hours to achieve a soft and puffy texture.
Maintain the frying oil around 190°C (375°F) so the bhature puff properly without becoming greasy.
Finish the chole with ghee and fresh lime juice for a richer restaurant-style flavor.
